items.title: Grafana Labs’ First Executive Briefing Center Coming to Ginza
items.summary: Grafana Labs does not have a headquarters office. Since its founding in 2014, it has been fully remote-first.It began with three co-founders living on different continents, and today our team spans more than 50 countries.From day one, the organization was designed with the assumption that everyone works remotely. Real-time meetings are kept to a minimum, information is shared through documentation, and we have cultivated a culture that trusts people to “work autonomously.” At its core lies the transparency and autonomy of open source.And now, we are building the world’s first Executive Briefing Center (EBC) in Ginza, Tokyo.A remote-first company creating a physical space—what does that mean?This article is the first in a three-part series following the EBC launch project.From the background of the concept to site selection, design philosophy, and even the demolition process, we will walk you through the journey.Not an “office,” but an “EBC”We do not call this place an “office.” It is an Executive Briefing Center, or EBC for short.As a remote-first company, there is no need to commute to a fixed location every day. However, there has never been a place anywhere in the world where people can directly experience the Grafana product, or share the same physical space with customers and the community to engage with technology. The EBC is designed to serve three roles.A place to experience the productA space where customers can directly interact with Grafana solutions, experiencing how observability solves real challenges through demos and briefings—not through a screen, but through face-to-face conversations in the same space.A starting point for innovationA flexible space design that is not bound by fixed layouts, allowing the environment to adapt to different purposes and foster new ideas and use cases.A hub for the communityA venue open for meetups and technical events, where people in the Grafana community can naturally gather and connect.We are building the world’s first EBC in Japan—to meet the rapidly growing demand for observability in the Japanese market. And for the Grafana community that already exists here, having a physical hub carries significant meaning.Because Grafana Labs is a company where employees around the world operate autonomously, we believe there is real value in creating a space for experiences that can only happen in person. We aim to create an open space—one where people feel that we are close to them.Site selection — A space that embodies our cultureTwo key requirements for the locationThe search for a property began around April 2025. Led by Country Manager Andy Schwabecher, we explored multiple areas. There were two key requirements in the selection process.First, the location needed to make customers feel that Grafana Labs is “right there with them.” It had to be open, accessible, and easy to drop by—a place where people could naturally engage with the Grafana solution. Not a space hidden behind security gates and reception procedures, but one that feels open and inviting. A building where customers might think, “Let’s just stop by.”Second, the space needed to embody the way Grafana Labs works. For us, the concept of an “office” is fundamentally different from that of a typical Japanese company. It is not a place where people sit at assigned desks every day. It must be an open, flexible environment that does not contradict a remote-first way of working. It also needed to accommodate a skeleton ceiling and allow for a design that breaks away from conventional office norms.Finding a place that satisfied both conditions was not easy.A property once lost—and eventually securedAround the summer of 2025, a building in Ginza was introduced by a broker. At the viewing stage, the team rated it highly, and it met all the conditions. However, during the consideration process, another tenant moved ahead, and the opportunity slipped away.While continuing to search for other options, we received news a few months later that the original tenant had withdrawn, and the space was available again.And so, after a long journey, we secured the current floor—about nine months after starting the search in April 2025.Looking back, not compromising on finding a place that could physically express Grafana Labs’ culture—transparency, openness, and autonomy—was one of the most important decisions in shaping the EBC.Design philosophy — Expressing Grafana’s culture through spaceSkeleton ceiling and open interiorIn a typical office or tenant space, ceilings are finished, and pipes and wiring are hidden.At the EBC, we chose the opposite: a full skeleton ceiling. Exposed pipes and visible wiring.
